summary: Re-fire targeting the one residual blocking finding from the prior instance (generated 2026-07-26): the Attribution-line prose still read '...corroborating multi-session parallelism as a productivity unlock generally, not the specific "worktrees" framing' -- reusing the coined phrase 'productivity unlock' (sourced only from the X thread) to describe what the Pragmatic Engineer interview corroborates, contradicting the maintainer's own newly-added guard two lines below. Current working-tree content (confirmed via `git diff -- <file>` against HEAD a90c9ec) has changed the clause to: 'corroborating parallel-session workflows generally, not the "productivity unlock" framing or the "worktrees" word.' This fully resolves the finding -- it now explicitly excludes BOTH coined phrases ('productivity unlock' AND 'worktrees') from what the interview corroborates, matching the fix_hint the prior instance proposed almost verbatim and mirroring the careful wording already present in the per-source freshness-stamp lines below it. Live re-verification performed today (2026-07-26): (1) X-thread oEmbed round-trip reproduces the verbatim quote -- 'Spin up 3-5 git worktrees at once, each running its own Claude session in parallel. It's the single biggest productivity unlock...' -- author Boris Cherny, dated January 31, 2026, confirming 'productivity unlock' is worktree-specific and X-thread-only exactly as the file now claims; (2) live WebFetch full-text scan of the Pragmatic Engineer piece confirms zero occurrences of 'worktree'/'worktrees'/'productivity unlock', confirms byline Gergely Orosz (published March 4, 2026), and confirms it only reports a raw metric -- 'Boris ships 20-30 PRs a day by running 5 parallel Claude instances... across five terminal tabs (each a separate checkout)' -- never characterizing the practice as a 'productivity unlock,' matching the file's own stamp line. Both URLs return HTTP 200. No other rule surface changed: the file's body (everything above `<!-- maintainer -->`) is byte-identical to the prior audit and contains zero **Prompt** fenced blocks or {{prompt:<key>}} markers (confirmed via `node scripts/expand-md.js` -- no-op, output identical to source), so check_prompts.md and the check_pedagogy.md technical sub-rules remain N/A, and every check_platform_and_boundaries.md platform-capability finding carries over unchanged. One informational (non-blocking) item persists unchanged from the prior instance: the file remains uncommitted (`git status --short` shows ' M', diff against a90c9ec includes both this fix and the earlier source-verification-section fix) and the Quality line's SHA pins (b3143a4) reference a commit that predates both fixes -- `git show b3143a4:<file>` still shows the original unfixed, unlabeled, unsplit Attribution line and no Source-verification section at all. Per check_platform_and_boundaries.md §24a this is a stamp/recordkeeping issue, not a content-correctness defect, so it stays non-blocking; content should be committed before any Quality re-stamp lands.
